title: [Keyboard Manager] Only apply to a specific app not available for non-chorded key triggers

status.label: Preserve app scoping when changing to a single-key trigger
status.detail: On PowerToys 0.100.0, a user reports that enabling app scoping through a chord and then changing to a single-key shortcut leaves the action active in other apps.

judgment.rationale: The original report says the app-specific checkbox is unavailable for a single-key trigger. A commenter on 0.100.0 reports that enabling it with a chord and then changing to a single-key trigger leaves the remap unscoped despite the UI suggesting otherwise. The broader open feature request #6756 asks for per-app single-key remapping, but this newer report adds a concrete mismatch between the displayed scope and actual behavior after changing the trigger.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.98.1 and says the specific-app option is disabled for non-chorded triggers.
A commenter reports the issue on 0.99.1.
A second commenter reports on 0.100.0 that enabling app scoping with a chord and then changing to a single-key shortcut leaves the remap active outside the selected app.
Open issue #6756 tracks the broader feature request for app-specific key remapping.
judgment.recommended_action: Ensure the UI and engine agree on whether a single-key remap is app-scoped; if the mapping is unsupported, do not silently present it as scoped after the trigger changes.

fix_assessment.rationale: The 0.100.0 report identifies a concrete UI/behavior mismatch after a supported chord-based setting is changed to a single-key trigger. The implementation should either enforce the displayed app scope or clearly prevent the invalid configuration.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep single-key remaps consistent with the displayed app scope
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The editor may retain or display an app-specific scope after a chord trigger is changed to a single-key trigger even though the engine does not enforce that scope.
plan: Reproduce the chord-to-single-key configuration transition on current stable and verify the actual process scope of the remap.
Align editor eligibility and persisted mapping state so an app-specific restriction is either applied to the single-key trigger or explicitly removed with a visible explanation.
Avoid changing the broader single-key per-app feature boundary tracked by #6756 without confirming intended support.
Add regression coverage for creating a scoped chord, changing it to a single-key trigger, saving, reopening the editor, and invoking the remap in another application.
verification: The editor never indicates a remap is app-specific when it applies in all applications.
Supported app-specific mappings remain restricted to the selected application after editing and reopening.
The UI consistently communicates the existing single-key per-app support boundary.

confidence.rationale: The 0.100.0 report documents a specific UI/behavior mismatch, but the intended single-key app-scope policy and current-build behavior should be confirmed before choosing between enforcement and preventing the misleading configuration.

issue_context.summary: The app-specific option is unavailable for single-key triggers, and a chord-to-single-key workaround reportedly leaves the mapping active in all apps despite the UI indicating a scope.
known_information: The original report lists PowerToys 0.98.1 and describes the disabled app-specific option for single-key triggers.
A commenter reports the same limitation on PowerToys 0.99.1.
A PowerToys 0.100.0 commenter says changing a scoped chord to a single-key trigger leaves the remap active outside the selected app.
Open issue #6756 tracks app-specific remapping for keys as a feature request.
inferences: The editor may retain stale scope state that is not enforced by the remapping engine after the trigger changes.
issue_context.analysis: The missing single-key app-specific capability is separately tracked by #6756. The current issue's distinct actionable point is that the chord-to-single-key workaround can display a scope that the engine does not apply; validate and fix that consistency without silently expanding feature scope.
initial_investigation: Read the issue body and all three comments, including the 0.100.0 report that the workaround is not actually scoped.
Reviewed open issue #6756; it captures the broader app-specific single-key remapping request rather than the newer scope-state mismatch.

information_gaps.information: Whether the chord-to-single-key scope mismatch still occurs on current stable and whether the editor continues to display the selected application after saving
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes an active scope-enforcement defect from a stale UI state or a deliberate unsupported single-key feature.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Repeat the reported chord-to-single-key edit on current stable, save and reopen the mapping, then test it in the selected app and a different app.

actions.label: Confirm app scope after changing the trigger

comment.body: A PowerToys 0.100.0 commenter reported that enabling the app-specific option with a chord and then changing the trigger to a single key leaves the remap active in other apps despite the UI. Could you confirm whether this still happens on current stable after saving and reopening the mapping?

actions.label: Reproduce app scope after a trigger change

reproduce.title: Check single-key remap scope after editing a chord
prerequisites: Two applications available for the scope comparison
setup: Create a chord-based remap restricted to one application.
steps: Change the source trigger from a chord to a single key.
Save the mapping and reopen it to check the displayed application scope.
Invoke the remap in the selected application.
Invoke the same source key in a different application.
reproduce.expected_result: The persisted mapping's displayed scope matches its actual behavior; it either remains restricted to the selected app or is clearly shown as unscoped.
